_comment: Served checkpoints. arch says which code reads a checkpoint: video_swin_b (the default, detector.py) or dfd_fcg (dfd_fcg.py). For the Video Swin-B models, temperature/threshold come from each '<name> - operating point.json' (validation temperature scaling + max-Youden threshold on the calibrated probability) and frame_spacing_s = median per-video frame spacing of that model's training split (preprocessing_materialization_v001.parquet). Vidi is DFD-FCG (Han et al., CVPR 2025; the authors' published checkpoint, trained on FaceForensics++ C23, research use only): it has no validation run of ours, so it is read at its own decision rule (temperature 1, threshold 0.5), and its frame_spacing_s is the spacing of its 10 training frames over 3 seconds.

weights_source._comment: Private Backblaze B2 bucket; workers download each checkpoint at start with a read-only key (B2_KEY_ID / B2_APP_KEY) and verify its SHA-1. These are byte-identical to the local checkpoint files. DFD-FCG.ckpt is weights.ckpt from the authors' checkpoint.zip, unchanged.

policy._comment: Frozen thesis preprocessing policy preprocessing_v001 (configs/preprocessing/policy_v001.yaml, hash 5610fc20...5632). Do not change.

dfd_fcg._comment: DFD-FCG (arch dfd_fcg). landmarks: the 2D-FAN TorchScript file of face_alignment 1.4.1, which the Dockerfile downloads into the image. Clips are 10 frames; each phase is tiled with clip_stride_in_phase. batch_clips_*: clips per pass through the CLIP ViT-L/14 encoder (>=20 GB cards / smaller cards / CPU).

whole_video._comment: Every decoded frame is analysed. Frames are split into k interleaved phases (k = round(frame_spacing_s x fps)) so each 16-frame clip has the trained spacing; each phase is tiled with clip_stride_in_phase. Clips never bridge face gaps longer than max_gap_factor x spacing. Videos above max_frames are subsampled evenly.

inference._comment: Swin clips per GPU batch (>=20 GB cards / smaller cards / CPU), FaceNet batch, pixel budget per face-detection batch, and GPU decoding. gpu_decode is off: torchcodec's CPU decoder is bit-identical to the thesis's PyAV rgb24 frames, while its GPU decoder (NVDEC, or on hosts where NVDEC declines a video its CPU fallback with GPU colour conversion) differs by up to 2/255 and is not safe with the per-scan CUDA streams of detector.ScanGate.

heatmap._comment: Evidence maps: exact final-stage token contributions for the top_k most suspicious clips (spread over the video) + the least suspicious, oriented toward the verdict, rendered and JPEG-encoded on the GPU. Shown relative to this video: values at or below low_percentile are clear, high_percentile is full strength.
